message.content:
Based on my research, here are three excellent seven-day China itinerary options depending on your interests:

---

## Option 1: Classic First-Timer Route — **Beijing + Shanghai**

This is the most recommended route for first-time visitors, balancing imperial history with modern China.

| Day | Location | Highlights |
|-----|----------|------------|
| 1 | **Beijing** | Arrive, evening neighborhood exploration in Dongcheng/Chaoyang |
| 2 | **Beijing** | Tiananmen Square → Forbidden City → Jingshan Park sunset views |
| 3 | **Beijing** | Temple of Heaven → Hutong walking tour → Lama Temple |
| 4 | **Beijing** | Great Wall at **Mutianyu** (less crowded than Badaling) → Ming Tombs |
| 5 | **Beijing → Shanghai** | Morning G-train (4.5–5.5 hours) → Evening Bund stroll |
| 6 | **Shanghai** | Yu Garden → French Concession → Nanjing Road → Bund night views |
| 7 | **Shanghai** | Oriental Pearl Tower or Shanghai Museum → Departure |

**Best for:** First-time visitors wanting iconic highlights without excessive travel

---

## Option 2: Classic Golden Triangle — **Beijing + Xi'an + Shanghai**

More packed but covers China's "must-sees" across 2,000+ years of history.

| Day | Location | Highlights |
|-----|----------|------------|
| 1 | **Beijing** | Arrive, evening exploration |
| 2 | **Beijing** | Forbidden City → Summer Palace → Peking duck dinner |
| 3 | **Beijing** | Great Wall (Mutianyu) → Ming Tombs |
| 4 | **Beijing → Xi'an** | Morning flight → Evening Muslim Quarter food tour |
| 5 | **Xi'an** | Terracotta Army (full day) → Ancient City Wall bike ride |
| 6 | **Xi'an → Shanghai** | Morning flight → Pudong skyline → Bund evening walk |
| 7 | **Shanghai** | Yu Garden → Departure |

**Best for:** Travelers wanting maximum iconic sights; note this is fast-paced with 2 domestic flights

---

## Option 3: East China Cultural Route — **Shanghai + Suzhou + Hangzhou**

Relaxed pace, garden culture, and scenic beauty without long-distance travel.

| Day | Location | Highlights |
|-----|----------|------------|
| 1–3 | **Shanghai** | The Bund → Yu Garden → French Concession → 798 Art District → local neighborhoods |
| 4 | **Suzhou** (day trip or overnight) | Classical gardens (Humble Administrator's Garden) → Pingjiang Road canals |
| 5–7 | **Hangzhou** | West Lake boat cruise → Longjing tea villages → Lingyin Temple → leisurely lake time |

**Best for:** Those preferring gardens, water towns, and relaxed pacing with easy 30-minute train hops

---

## Practical Tips for All Itineraries

| Topic | Advice |
|-------|--------|
| **Best time to visit** | Spring (April–May) or Autumn (September–November) |
| **Visa (2026)** | Many nationalities qualify for **240-hour visa-free transit** or **30-day unilateral visa-free** entry—confirm based on your passport |
| **Getting around** | High-speed rail (G-trains) for city-to-city; metro systems excellent in major cities |
| **Daily budget** | USD $50–100 depending on style |
| **Essential prep** | Download VPN before arrival, carry cash (many places don't take cards), install Google Translate for menus |
| **Book ahead** | Forbidden City tickets (sell out!), weekend/holiday train tickets |

---

## My Recommendation

- **First trip, want icons:** Choose **Option 1** (Beijing + Shanghai)
- **Want Terracotta Warriors too:** Choose **Option 2** (Golden Triangle) — but be prepared for a busy week
- **Prefer relaxed, scenic, cultural depth:** Choose **Option 3** (Shanghai-Suzhou-Hangzhou)

---

Sources:
1. https://startchinatravel.com/7-day-china-itinerary-first-timers-2026/
2. https://wonderplan.ai/itineraries/china/7-days
3. https://www.explorewithshanghai.com/hub-east-china-itinerary-7-days/
